Research question: "What measurements or analyses would best reveal why a small fraction of genetically identical cancer cells survive targeted drug treatment?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Lineage barcoding to test whether survival is bimodal and inherited
ideas.description: Label each cell with a heritable DNA barcode, expose the population to the drug, and check whether surviving clones were already present and sized before treatment. If survival is a bimodal, pre-existing trait, survivors will share barcodes with pre-treatment clones; if it is a stochastic, reversible switch, survivors will be spread across many barcodes with no pre-treatment enrichment.

ideas.title: Pre-treatment single-cell profiling of the 'subnivean' state
ideas.description: Run paired scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq on the untreated parental population, then score each cell's pre-existing expression and chromatin signature against its later survival, using barcodes or sorted reporter cells to link the two. This finds any sheltered state (for example slow cycling or a particular chromatin configuration) that predisposes cells to persist beneath the drug's pressure.

ideas.title: Live-cell reporters of signaling and cell-cycle dynamics during drug exposure
ideas.description: Use time-lapse imaging with a FUCCI cell-cycle reporter and a kinase translocation reporter (for example ERK or AKT activity) to follow individual cells through the drug pulse. Test whether cells that eventually survive show distinct pathway rebound, a delayed cell cycle entry, or a transient signaling dip before the drug takes effect.

ideas.title: Re-challenge and metabolic profiling of sorted survivors
ideas.description: Sort the surviving cells, release them from drug for several passages, then re-challenge them to measure whether tolerance is heritable or reverts. In parallel, run Seahorse respirometry and metabolomics on survivors versus sensitive cells to see whether they hold a stable internal metabolic setpoint (like a hematherm regulating its own temperature) that buffers the drug's effects.

ideas.title: Pooled CRISPR screen with single-cell readout to find survival regulators
ideas.description: Run a genome-wide CRISPR knockout screen under drug, comparing sequenced guide representation in survivors versus treated bulk, and pair this with single-cell readouts to see which knockouts change the probability of survival rather than just its magnitude. Hits that rewire the tumor's core rules (an antinomian-like defiance of the drug's logic, such as chromatin regulators or stress-response genes) would point to the mechanisms that make some cells persist.
